request.spec:
Every change that alters any person's claimed or due-total is followed in the audit, after the
change's own lines, by one line per person whose figures changed: ROLLUP name=<name>
claimed=<claimed> due-total=<due-total>, people in the order they were added, a person who did
not exist before the change counting as changed; then, when the sheet's claimed-total or
due-total changed, one line TOTALS claimed-total=<total> due-total=<total>. A change that moves
no figure adds no such line (setting a rate to the value it already has, settling a claim whose
frozen figure equals its live one, re-stating a person whose figures did not move). Changing the
sheet's today is a change like any other and is followed by these lines when figures move, with
no line of its own.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Every change that alters any person's claimed or due-total is followed in the audit, after the

claimed=<claimed> due-total=<due-total>, people in the order they were added, a person who did
not exist before the change counting as changed; then, when the sheet's claimed-total or
due-total changed, one line TOTALS claimed-total=<total> due-total=<total>. A change that moves
no figure adds no such line (setting a rate to the value it already has, settling a claim whose
frozen figure equals its live one, re-stating a person whose figures did not move). Changing the

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The rollup audit lines are in place, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 acceptance tests.

**How it works**
- **Working out the figures:** `RollupService` (`src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/rollup/`) calculates each person's claimed and due-total the same way the screen does. That includes `n/a` when a person's grade has no rate on the sheet's today and none of their claims has a settled or stated figure. It also works out the sheet's claimed-total and due-total, skipping `n/a`.
- **Before and after:** every change now has two extra steps. `SnapshotRollup` records the figures just before anything is written. `AuditRollup` runs after the change's own audit line and compares.
  - It writes one `ROLLUP` line for each person whose figures moved, in the order people were added. A new person always gets a line.
  - It then writes `TOTALS` if either sheet total moved.
  - A change that moves nothing adds no lines. A refused change fails before the rollup step, so it writes nothing either.
- **Where it's added:** adding or editing a person, adding or editing a claim, opening/settling/voiding a claim, taking a statement, setting a rate, and changing the sheet's today. Today changes get rollup lines only, with no line of their own.

**Two things that differ from what you might expect**
- **Field name:** the change request writes `ROLLUP name=<name>`, but the test expects `person=<name>`, so I used `person=`. Every line also starts with `sheet=… by=…`, as the other audit records do.
- **Today change sends the user:** the "set today" request didn't send who made it, so I added `?user=` to it in `SheetToday.tsx`. Without this, its rollup lines would have no `by=`.

**Limitation:** if two users change the same sheet at exactly the same moment, a rollup line could compare against slightly stale "before" figures. The tests don't do this, and I added no locking for it.
